composers_checked.name: Haydn, Joseph
composers_checked.note: Formations winds-strings, continuo, other and piano-trio. Gap check against Wikipedia's work list (after Grove) for Hob. II, IV, XIV and XV and against complete recorded sets: Beaux Arts Trio's complete trios (Philips 432 061-2), Haydn Sinfonietta Wien's Complete Early Divertimenti (BIS-CD-1806/08), the Divine Art Notturni & Scherzandi, and the keyboard divertimenti and concertini of L'Arte dell'Arco (Brilliant) and Ensemble Melkus (Claves). Haydn has no continuo works in scope; the Op. 3 trios are string trios (c25).

note: Haydn, mixed ensembles and piano trios: complete. Where the brief was unclear or a judgement call was needed: (1) Keyboard: Hob. XIV parts ('cembalo') entered as piano with harpsichord as alternative, so XIV:3 and XIV:13 move from the census's 'other' to piano-strings. (2) Hob. XV:15-17 were written for flute, cello and keyboard (Wikipedia/Grove, Bland 1790): flute is the main part, violin the alternative, so they derive as winds-strings. They are 'Piano Trios' by title and in the Beaux Arts cycle. Swap if the owner wants them under piano trio. Hob. IV:6-11 also keep flute as the main part (IMSLP: '2 violins (or flute, violin), cello'). (3) Notturni Hob. II:25-32 are entered in Haydn's London version (flute and oboe, or two flutes, for the two lire organizzate; the lira is not in the vocabulary). (4) Scherzandi Hob. II:33-38: Wikipedia says 'orchestra', but the scoring is eight single parts and the only recording found (Divine Art) is by chamber ensembles. Kept at medium confidence; the owner may drop them. (5) Concertini Hob. XIV:11-13 (flag concerto?) are kept: Hob. XIV is Haydn's keyboard-divertimento group, and two chamber ensembles recorded them for keyboard, two violins and bass. The booklets were not checked for one player to a part. The Concertino Hob. XVIII:F2 (same scoring, on the Brilliant disc) is not added because it belongs to the concerto group and has a letter number. (6) Wrong outOfScope reason: the Cassations Hob. II:21 and II:22 are 'Divertimenti a sei stromenti' (two horns, two violins, viola, bass; BIS booklet), not string orchestra. They are added with gap:true and their IMSLP pages. (7) The census missed four IMSLP pages entirely (neither candidates nor outOfScope): Hob. II:1, II:8, II:20 and II:G1. They are added with gap:true. Scorings come from the BIS booklet, whose titles (Haydn's own: 'a cinque', 'a sei', 'a nove stromenti') confirm one player to a part. Hob. II:11: IMSLP lists cello and bass, the BIS booklet one 'basso', so it is entered as five players. (8) Doubtful works kept because they are recorded under Haydn's name, each marked in notes or with medium confidence: Op. 5 Nos. 1-3 and 5 (Hob. II:D9, G4, D10, D11; Kuijken Ensemble, Accent), Hob. XV:C1 (also attributed to Wagenseil), XV:f1, II:G1, II:D22 and XIV:13 ('probably authentic', Grove). (9) Piano Trio Hob. XIV:6 comes from the 1767 Hummel print ('6 Keyboard Trios', where IMSLP marks it 'arr.' of the Partita Hob. XVI:6). The Beaux Arts Trio recorded it as Landon's trio No. 3. Medium confidence. (10) Not added: XV:C2 (doubtful, no recording found), XV:33 and XV:D1 (lost), the Beaux Arts 'Piano Trio in D, Hob. deest' (status unclear, one track), II:24 (a fragment per Henle/BIS), XIV:5 (fragment) and XIV:10 (scoring unknown). Op. 5 Nos. 4 and 6 are not added either: they are arrangements by an unknown hand of Hob. II:1 and II:11, which are kept. (11) Outside my formations but unowned: the Cassation Hob. II:2 for two violins, two violas and bass (a string quintet, recorded on BIS) has no Haydn slice. (12) Trios have set null, following benchmark 100077 (the publishers' opus numbers conflict). Years follow Wikipedia/Grove (XV:21-23 '1794-95' where IMSLP has 1792). Minutes are the Beaux Arts timings, other works their cited recording. No benchmark issue: XV:25 runs 16'46" with the Beaux Arts, 15 in the benchmark, within the usual range. (13) floor.published is left blank: all floors are commercial recordings. Levels are calibrated on the benchmark XV:25 = 4. Early trios are 3 (piano about ABRSM 6). The flashiest late trios (XV:14, 27, 28, 30) and the horn trio Hob. IV:5 are 5.
